text.title: Retro Facilitation Multistyle Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every retro facilitation multistyle application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: `format` MUST be one of `mad-sad-glad`, `4ls`, `sailboat`, `lean-coffee`, `anonymous-async`. When `team_state.distribution` is `async`, the format MUST be `anonymous-async`. `lean-coffee` is allowed only when `distribution` is `in-person` or `hybrid` with every participant on a live call. `mad-sad-glad` MUST NOT be used with an `async` team.

rationale.source: Derby and Larsen, Agile Retrospectives (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2006); widely established practice in distributed-team facilitation

rule.rationale: A live card-sorting format run across UA, PT and UK timezones is a retro for whoever is in the overlap hour; the outsourced half posts nothing and the action list reflects one office. Lean-coffee's dot-voting needs everyone watching the same board at the same moment, which is exactly the thing an async team does not have.

rule.statement: `selection_rationale` MUST be at least 20 characters and MUST state the `distribution`, the `fatigue_signal` and the formats used in the previous two retros. "We always do this one", "team likes it" or a rationale that does not mention team state is rejected.

rationale.source: Derby and Larsen, Agile Retrospectives (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2006), choosing activities per context

rule.rationale: The rationale is the only record of why this format was chosen for this team on this date. Without it the quarterly review cannot tell whether the format drove low participation or the team did, and the next facilitator inherits a habit instead of a decision.

rule.statement: When `team_state.fatigue_signal` is `fatigued`, `format` MUST differ from the formats recorded in the previous two retro instances. When it is `rotating`, `format` MUST differ from the previous retro's format. The same format three times in a row is allowed only with `fatigue_signal: fresh` and a rationale that cites participation evidence (card count or attendance at or above the previous retro).

rationale.source: Widely established practice in agile facilitation (retro fatigue); Retromat activity library

rule.rationale: Teams that run the same three columns for a year produce the same three complaints and stop filling the third column. Rotation is cheap and the fatigue signal is what makes it a rule rather than a whim; the participation-evidence exception keeps a format that is demonstrably working.

rule.statement: Every retro MUST open with Kerth's Prime Directive read aloud or posted, followed by an anonymous safety check on a 1-5 scale before any discussion. If the safety median is below 3, the facilitator MUST switch the remainder to anonymous input (cards or form) for that session and record the switch in the instance. A line manager who is not a team member MUST NOT attend the discussion portion.

rationale.source: Kerth, Project Retrospectives: A Handbook for Team Reviews (Dorset House, 2001); Derby and Larsen, Agile Retrospectives (2006), safety check activity

rule.rationale: A retro with a manager in the room and no safety check becomes a status meeting where the loudest voice reports and the rest nod. The safety check costs ninety seconds and tells the facilitator, before it matters, whether the format they chose can produce anything true.

rule.statement: Before collecting new input, the facilitator MUST walk the previous instance's `action_items` and record each as done, not done, or dropped with a reason; this sets `outcome_review.last_run_at` to the current `retro_date`. An action not done MAY be carried over at most once; on the second miss it is dropped with a recorded reason, not re-listed. An instance whose previous actions have no recorded status is invalid.

rationale.source: Scrum Guide (2020), Sprint Retrospective; Derby and Larsen, Agile Retrospectives (2006), closing the retrospective

rule.rationale: The single most common retro complaint is "we said this last time". Reviewing status first turns the retro into a loop with memory: actions that keep not happening reveal a constraint worth discussing, and actions nobody wants to drop reveal that the owner was never real.

rule.statement: Each instance MUST produce between 1 and 3 `action_items`. Every item MUST have `owner` set to one named person (not "team", "everyone" or a channel), an `evidence_link` to a tracker issue or PR created for that action, and a `due_date` no later than the next retro. Items without an evidence link at the end of the retro are recorded as discussion notes, not actions.

rationale.source: Scrum Guide (2020): the most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible; widely established practice in agile coaching

rule.rationale: Eight action items owned by "the team" produce zero changes and one demoralised facilitator. One to three items with a person, a ticket and a date produce something to review next time, which is the whole reason the outcome-review field exists.

rule.statement: For `anonymous-async`, cards MUST be collected through a form or board that stores no author identity, over a window that includes at least one full working day in every participant's timezone. The facilitator MUST cluster cards into themes before the recap and MUST NOT attribute, quote by name, or ask "who wrote this". The recap discussion is held live only if every timezone can attend or is recorded and open for comment for a further working day.

rationale.source: GitLab Handbook, asynchronous communication guidance; widely established practice in anonymous feedback collection

rule.rationale: The anonymity is what buys the outsourced developer's honest card about the client's deploy window. One "who put this one?" in the recap and the next retro's board is empty. The timezone-spanning window is what makes the format async rather than a live retro with a form attached.

rule.statement: The instance MUST state a total timebox before the retro starts: at most 3 hours for a one-month iteration and proportionally shorter for shorter iterations (45-90 minutes for a two-week sprint is the working range). For `lean-coffee`, topics MUST be dot-voted before discussion and each topic timeboxed, with a visible vote to extend; a topic MUST NOT run past two extensions. Overrunning the timebox is recorded in the instance and counts toward the `fatigue_signal` at the next retro.

rationale.source: Scrum Guide (2020), Sprint Retrospective timebox; Lean Coffee format (Benson and Westbrook, 2009)

rule.rationale: Unbounded retros are the fastest route to `fatigued`. The timebox is also a fairness device: without the per-topic clock and vote, lean-coffee becomes the two most senior people's conversation with an audience.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit an artefact passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions hold.

rule.statement: Skip; surface the missing precondition; do not synthesize.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.
